title: Termination conditions written into an Accord operate as consent given in advance
content:
A.2.8.3.2.4 resolves what would otherwise be a circularity. If mutual consent is required for every termination, then an Accord clause saying "this Accord ends if X" would be unenforceable without the parties re-consenting at the moment X occurs — letting a party defeat a condition it had already accepted.

The provision closes this: "[t]he parties' agreement to those conditions, as expressed in the Accord, constitutes their consent to action taken in accordance with them." Core GovOps then "gives effect to such a change by incorporating it into the Atlas."

The design consequence is that Accord drafting is where counterparties should place their real protections and Sky its real triggers. A condition negotiated into the text at signing is self-executing; anything left to later negotiation is subject to veto. This rewards specificity at drafting time and makes vague Accords structurally rigid.

Note also what Core GovOps is doing here: it is not deciding anything, only recording an outcome the Accord already determined. The Atlas Edit becomes ministerial, which is the same pattern as Genesis Capital transfers proceeding straight to an Executive Vote — the decision was made when the text was written.
description: Where an Accord specifies its own modification or termination conditions, acting on them needs no fresh consent — the parties' agreement to the conditions IS their consent to the outcome.
